newsitem.title: USA: Washington state lawmakers approve tax referendum.
newsitem.headline: Washington state lawmakers approve tax referendum.

text.p: The Washington Legislature on Wednesday approved a measure that would allow the state's voters to decide how much to cut property taxes.

The state House voted 60-38 to place a referendum on the November ballot asking citizens whether they want to make a modest cut in the state property tax and limit future tax increases to the rate of inflation.
The Senate approved the referendum plan on Monday.
Earlier attempts by the Republican-controlled Legislature to pass the tax reductions into law were swiftly vetoed by Democratic Gov. Gary Locke.
Republican Rep. Mike Carrell predicted easy passage by voters in November. By law, Locke cannot block the referendum.
"Property taxes are doubling every eight years, and none of the solutions, other than this, even approach solving that problem," Carrell said.

Washingtonians will decide whether to make a permanent cut of 4.7 percent in the state property tax levy. Then they will be asked to cap annual increases in state and local property tax collections at the rate of inflation.
Minority Democrats accused lawmakers of taking the easy way out.
"Halfway through the session, we are throwing up our hands and were asking the voters to do our job for us, to make decisions," said Rep. Hans Dunshee. "We should compromise with the governor."

Shortly after the property tax vote, the Legislature set up another tax-cut showdown with Locke by approving a rollback in business taxes. The state House voted 91-7 to return the state's business and occupation tax on service businesses to pre-1993 levels.
In 1993, the Legislature raised that tax on architects, accountants, consultants and lawyers, among others, as much as 66 percent to close an unexpected budget deficit.
Locke endorsed the tax rollback during last fall's election campaign but now is hedging on whether the state can afford to forego $202 million in tax revenue.
